title: Some blocks in the video are drawn wrong (luanti 15821, Attempt12)
verdict_reason: Every dimension holds. **Difficulty meets Option A**: no-image 0/3 (`KNSxx3s`, `hxqbksk`, `wwL8dZA`) and with-image exactly 1/4 (`AEURini` 1.0, 9/9 f2p + 9/9 p2p; `Ri5pb59`, `dMNNnzm`, `tnZgnKu` fail). Attempt12 differs from the reviewed Attempt8 only in `instruction.md`, `task.toml` (title, difficulty text), and the asset description in `ASSET_MANIFEST.json` / `evidence_bundle.json`. `environment/` (Dockerfile, bugs, recording.mp4), `solution/` and `tests/` are byte-identical, so the Attempt8 local oracle 1.0 / nop 0.0 / identical re-run still apply, and the CB oracle/nop for Attempt12 match them. Symptom Specificity stays a non-fail 3 (`[Non-Fail - Image-carried Symptom]`): the element types are now named, but the linked-block and shaped-block defects are stated only as categories, and the exact defects are left to the clip.

All 11 fixed files present and non-empty: `task.toml` (5515 B), `instruction.md` (1239 B), `evidence_bundle.json` (995 B), `environment/Dockerfile` (2970 B), `environment/assets/ASSET_MANIFEST.json` (606 B), `solution/fix.patch` (5364 B), `solution/solve.sh` (349 B), `tests/config.json` (1882 B), `tests/test.patch` (25168 B), `tests/test.sh` (10434 B), `tests/verifier.py` (6623 B). `json.load` passes on all JSON files; `tomllib` parses `task.toml`; `verifier.py` is unchanged from Attempt8 (py_compile passed there). `recording.mp4` is the same file (sha256 `bcc16a63…`): h264 1280x720, 30 fps, 63.0 s. Extras: `environment/bugs/bug_01..06.patch` and `README.md`, not a fail.

dimensions.name: Structure – Deliverables & Packaging

dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Note: when submitting, package `Tasks/` and `Trials/` as separate `Tasks.tar.gz` and `Trials.tar.gz` that unpack to those exact top-level folder names.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Requires Visual Evidence
dimensions.evidence: `instruction.md` points to `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4` (Dockerfile `COPY assets/recording.mp4 /app/.harbor_assets/`). Attempt12 now names element types ("Stairs, slabs and other shaped blocks", "A block that links up with its neighbours", "like the track" in What happens, "blocks that have a second picture painted over their main one", "a ladder or a sign fixed to a wall") but still no instance, direction, axis, file or mechanism. Which stairs face the wrong way (t≈25–31 s), which two rail corners bend wrong (t≈21 s), which window has bars at its joints (t≈45 s), which fence row is unjoined (t≈55 s), which wall's outline floats (t≈39–51 s), and that the track vanishes at a distance (t≈6 s) and the grass outline is hidden close up (t≈1 s) are only in the clip. Trials back this up (supporting only): all 3 no-image runs confirmed `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4: No such file or directory`, and all 3 found the overlay pull in `tile.cpp` but kept it as correct (`KNSxx3s`: "a depth-only nudge (-1/-1) on that layer, so it is never drawn nearer than its block"; `hxqbksk`: "I found no fault here"; `wwL8dZA`: "as far as I can recall that matches upstream"), so they failed the 3 overlay f2p. 3/4 with-image runs tied the vanishing track and dashed grass outline in the clip to that pull and removed it. Leak scan: no repo name, URL, org, issue/PR link, file list or code identifier.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Non-graded note: "nothing is drawn even slightly nearer than the surface it belongs to (this matters for blocks that have a second picture painted over their main one…)" is close to the mechanism, but it is a visible rule, and no text-only run turned it into the fix (0/3 on the overlay f2p).

dimensions.name: Instruction – Symptom Specificity
dimensions.evidence:
Prompt table (element | defect, text or image? | expected, text or image? | comparison pointed to | clue left to image | described correctly?):
1. "Stairs, slabs and other shaped blocks" | text gives only the category ("how some of them … are put together"); the actual defect (east/west stairs backwards, open X sides missing) is image-only | text: "face the way they were placed and are drawn whole, from every side" | none (correct counterparts are in the clip, not pointed to) | which block, which direction: image | yes.
2. "A block that links up with its neighbours" ("like the track" in What happens) | text: only "links to them correctly"; actual defects (two rail corners bent wrong, bars at the X window's joints, Z fence unjoined): image | text (generic) | none | which block, which axis: image | yes.
3. "what stays visible from close by and from far away" / blocks "that have a second picture painted over their main one" | text: "Nothing disappears into what it rests on" | text: "nothing is drawn even slightly nearer than the surface it belongs to" | none | what disappears (the track far away, the grass outline close up): image | yes.
4. "the box the game draws around the block the player points at", "a ladder or a sign fixed to a wall" | category in text; exact defect (box floating off the Z walls, outline on grass mostly hidden): image | text: "one closed box that fits around it" | none | which wall: image | yes.
The generic opener is followed at once by the element types and the expected rules, so the symptom-specificity check passes, and nothing is described incorrectly. Elements are now named by type (an improvement on Attempt8's "parts"), but for rows 1, 2 and 4 the defect is stated only as a category or as the negation of an expected rule, and the exact defect is carried by the clip. That is the Image-carried Symptom case (3), not a pass and not a fail.
Trajectory check (all 4 with-image runs): every run read the same symptom classes from the clip, and none took a visible defect for intended behaviour. `AEURini` found all seven. `Ri5pb59` fixed stairs, sides, rails, wall box and overlay, and never reached the glass or fence code (missed, not misread). `tnZgnKu` fixed six and missed only the X-row glass. `dMNNnzm` fixed all six injected bugs and read the clip's "things sinking" symptom, but attributed it to the stairs: it inspected the overlay offset and wrote "Overlay polygon offset and the shaders look correct" and "These are already pulled forward only in the depth test … so nothing is drawn nearer than its surface". That is a misdiagnosis of the cause in code by one run of four, not agents taking the pictured symptom for intended behaviour (the rubric's example is 3/4 runs calling a bug glint normal shine), so it does not trigger the fail clause.
dimensions.wrong: Element types are named, but the shaped-block, linked-block and outline defects are stated only as categories / negated rules ("put together", "links correctly", "one closed box that fits"). The exact defects are carried by the clip. Not a fail under V27; record as `[Non-Fail - Image-carried Symptom]`.
dimensions.fix: Optional, for a 5: state each defect in text without the cause, e.g. "some stairs face the wrong way and some shaped blocks are missing a side; some linked blocks join wrongly or not at all; the outline of a block fixed to a wall floats off it; the track and the outline on the grass are partly hidden". Caution: the task now sits exactly at Option A (1/4), and naming defects per type would likely make it easier, so weigh this against dimension 16. Any change to `instruction.md` changes the task checksum, so all 7 trials must be re-run.

dimensions.name: Instruction – Task Type
dimensions.evidence: `task_type = "visual_regression"` (Guidelines Step IV: decide which change is the accidental regression and reverse only that, keeping intended changes). The instruction describes drawing defects to fix and says "Everything else should keep looking as it does now". The defects are regressions against intact counterparts of the same kind in the same clip (the other stairs, the other window, the X-fence). Upstream issue 15821 is a regression of the overlay polygon offset. The text fits the type reasonably.

dimensions.name: Image – Evidence Quality
dimensions.evidence:
The asset is byte-identical to Attempt8 (sha256 `bcc16a63…`); only its `description` changed ("parts" -> "blocks"), which is still true. Naming table (file | role | what the frames show | what name/role/instruction claim | true? | agents confused?):
`recording.mp4` | `recording` | an uncut 63 s first-person clip of a devtest scene at the injected base: a track loop, stairs on a grass hill, a cobble house with framed-glass windows, ladder, sign and slab, and two fences; the camera stops on blocks so the outline appears | neutral name; description: "uncut 63-second player-eye clip … stops on one, so the game marks what the player is pointing at"; instruction: "Several things go wrong with the blocks in `recording.mp4`" | true (sha256 `bcc16a63…` = manifest; frames in `evidence/`) | no (no run treated the clip as the expected state).
Asset vs f2p, per defect (preconditions from `test.patch` → state in the clip → reachable?):
(1) 3 overlay f2p (`test_tile_polygon_offset.cpp`: a cube with an overlay on every side; `applyMaterialOptions` must not pull layer 1 toward the camera; a node without an overlay gets no offset) → grass ground with an overlay: the outline is drawn dashed or hidden at t≈1 s and the track lying on it is gone at t≈6 s → yes. Cross-check: the fix of what the clip shows (drop the pull on the overlay) passes all 3. Attempt12 trials confirm it: `tnZgnKu` removed the pull, `AEURini` and `Ri5pb59` kept the overlay at true depth and pushed only the base layer of overlay blocks back; all three pass the 3 overlay f2p. `dMNNnzm` kept the pull and fails them, as it should.
(2) Framed glass along X (3-pane row along X; no frame at the joints, frame at both ends) → house window running along X shows bars at the pane joints (t≈45 s), while the Z window is clean → yes.
(3) facedir 1/3 node box (stair; node, selection and collision boxes plus the drawn top) → east/west stairs built backwards (t≈25–31 s), north/south fine → yes.
(4) Node box beside a full block on X (slab next to stone; the open opposite face must be drawn) → see-through stairs and slab sides (t≈25 s, t≈39–47 s) → yes.
(5) Rail curves +X+Z / −X−Z (UV corners turned by 90/270) → two corner kinds of the loop bend the wrong way (t≈21 s) → yes.
(6) Fence posts along Z (bars join the posts, nothing beyond) → the Z fence row stands as separate posts, while the X row is joined (t≈55 s vs t≈57 s) → yes.
(7) Wallmounted Z selection box (param2 4/5) → the outline of the ladder and sign on the Z walls floats on the far side of the node (t≈39–51 s), while the X-wall ladder is fine → yes.
Step 7 (injected defects): all 6 `environment/bugs/` defects appear in the clip. A fix that skips any of them leaves a visible defect in the clip on a supported drawtype (facedir node box, nodebox face culling, raillike, fencelike, glasslike_framed, wallmounted), so it would be an incomplete fix, not an alternative. Complete fix? Yes only with all 7.

dimensions.name: Metadata – task_type
dimensions.evidence: `visual_regression` is one of the seven valid values. The asset is one recording of the regressed state, with intact counterparts of each broken kind in the same clip; the rubric says not to penalize a valid choice even if another type fits better. The tags include `multimodal`, `visual_regression` and `Luanti`.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Non-graded note: the Step IV evidence column for `visual_regression` is a before/after pair. A single clip of the broken state would also fit `visual_bug_fix`.

dimensions.name: Evidence – Chain Consistency
dimensions.evidence: File `environment/assets/recording.mp4`: 10520876 B, sha256 `bcc16a63d102965661fdf419f5d2145b20c9feb4eaab4d24f685ea262b357513`. `ASSET_MANIFEST.json`: `file: recording.mp4`, same bytes and sha256, `container_path: /app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`. `evidence_bundle.json`: `local_path: /app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`, role `recording`, `source_kind: captured_from_repo` (an empty `url` is valid for captured evidence). `instruction.md` ref: `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4`. Dockerfile: `COPY assets/recording.mp4 /app/.harbor_assets/`. All four agree. Attempt12 changed only the `description` text in the manifest and bundle; names, sha256, bytes and paths are unchanged.

dimensions.name: Golden Fix – Applies Cleanly
dimensions.evidence: `solution/fix.patch`, `tests/test.patch` and `environment/bugs/*.patch` are byte-identical to Attempt8, where `git apply --check /solution/fix.patch` printed `APPLY_CHECK_OK` and `git apply --check /tests/test.patch` printed `TESTPATCH_CHECK_OK` in the QC-built image at `harbor_base`. The Attempt12 CB oracle reaches reward 1.0 (9/9, 9/9), which requires the patch to apply.

dimensions.name: Golden Fix – Source-Only Scope
dimensions.evidence: The `diff --git` paths in `fix.patch` are `src/client/content_mapblock.cpp`, `src/client/tile.cpp`, `src/client/tile.h`, `src/mapnode.cpp` and `src/nodedef.cpp`. That set equals `files_edited` exactly (compared in Python: True). No test, doc, lockfile or changeset path.

dimensions.name: Tests – Implementation Overfit
dimensions.evidence:
`tests/test.patch`, `tests/config.json`, `solution/fix.patch` are byte-identical to Attempt8. Value-level assertions are float comparisons on `SMaterial::PolygonOffsetSlopeScale` / `PolygonOffsetDepthBias` (`>= 0`, `overlay <= base`, `== 0` for a node without an overlay) and geometry checks with tolerances (`sameBoxes` is order-independent with EPS 1e-3; `covered` is point-in-triangle for either winding; `hasFace` checks normal and plane; rail corners are matched as pos+UV pairs in any vertex order; fence checks are bounds only). The accepted set is the material's float fields, which Irrlicht reads freely, so no string, enum or format spelling is involved.
Equivalence table (alternative | correct in repo context? | test accepts):
• golden: positive offset on layer 0 only when an overlay exists | yes | yes
• remove the overlay offset entirely | valid (meets every instruction rule) | yes, run by the verifier in `tnZgnKu` (Attempt12) and `79YZ3Xy`/`EuyuJbj` (Attempt8): all 3 overlay f2p pass
• keep the overlay at true depth, push only the base layer of overlay blocks back (new flag) | valid and plausible | yes, verified in `AEURini` (reward 1.0) and `Ri5pb59` (overlay f2p pass)
• remove the offset and draw the overlay with `ZBuffer = ECFN_LESSEQUAL` | valid and plausible | yes, verified in Attempt8 `2nxVxqj` (reward 1.0)
• a different positive magnitude on the base (e.g. bias 2, or bias only) when an overlay is present | valid | yes by inspection (only `>=`/`<=`)
• the offset applied where the mesh materials are built instead of in `applyMaterialOptions` | valid | yes by inspection (both layers return 0/0, and 0 <= 0)
• keep the pull on the overlay (`dMNNnzm` left it; Attempt8 `cqnZGh3`: slope 0, bias −1) | not valid: the instruction pins "nothing is drawn even slightly nearer than the surface it belongs to" | no (correctly rejected)
• push every base layer back | not valid: the instruction says "blocks without one are fine as they are", and upstream's own comment in the golden says it intrudes on the neighbour's overlay Z space | no (correctly rejected).
Geometry f2p: every Attempt12 run (with and without the clip) fixed facedir, nodebox dirs, rails and wallmounted its own way and passed those f2p. All trial failures are defects the run never fixed (glass, fence) or the pinned overlay pull. Fix only what the evidence shows: that is all 7 defects (see dimension 6), which equals the oracle.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Non-graded note: removing the offset entirely (no Z-fight guard between overlay and base) passes too. Unit tests can't tell it from the golden, and it meets the stated rules, so this is leniency, not overfit.

dimensions.name: Tests – f2p/p2p Identifier Validity
dimensions.evidence: `task.toml` `[metadata] f2p/p2p` and `tests/config.json` `f2p/p2p` compared in Python: identical (9 + 9, same order). Each ID is a Catch2 `TEST_CASE` name in `test.patch` (unchanged). Every Attempt12 `reward_detail.json` (7 trials, CB oracle, CB nop) has exactly 18 keys with `pass`/`fail` and no `missing` or `ambiguous`, so `verifier.py` resolves each ID once.

dimensions.name: Tests – p2p Classification
dimensions.evidence: All 9 p2p pass on nop and on oracle: Attempt12 CB `Nop` (`57SU4X7`) p2p 9/9, CB `Oracle` (`USS3TLX`) 9/9, and the Attempt8 local nop/oracle/re-run 9/9 on the byte-identical environment, solution and tests. All 7 Attempt12 trials also pass 9/9 p2p.

dimensions.name: Tests – Discriminating (f2p)
dimensions.evidence: All 9 f2p fail on nop and pass on oracle: Attempt12 CB `Nop` f2p 0/9 (all 9 listed as fail), CB `Oracle` 9/9; Attempt8 local nop 0/9 and oracle 9/9 in both runs on the identical environment/solution/tests. Each f2p matches one defect, with a paired p2p for the unaffected direction.

dimensions.name: Tests – Determinism
dimensions.evidence: The tests are pure CPU checks on generated meshes, node boxes and `SMaterial` fields. No GPU, timers, animation, randomness, fonts or network. `test.sh` installs nothing: it restores test paths from `harbor_base`, applies `test.patch`, runs an incremental `cmake --build` and runs `luanti --run-unittests` with a JUnit reporter. Since nothing is installed at test time, `[verifier] network_mode = "public"` raises no network-configuration issue. Oracle re-run: two local oracle runs gave identical `reward_detail.json` (18/18 pass), which is also identical to the CB oracle's. The local nop `reward_detail.json` is identical to the CB nop's. Attempt12 CB oracle `reward_detail.json` is again 18/18 pass, the same as both Attempt8 local oracle runs.
dimensions.wrong: Nothing found. Cosmetic note: `test.sh` passes `"${REPORTS[@]}"`, which is never defined. It expands to nothing and is harmless.

dimensions.name: Hardening – Difficulty (Model Trial Fails)
dimensions.evidence:
From `verifier/reward.txt` (job configs: `without_images` `n_attempts: 3`, `with_images` `n_attempts: 4`, both `anthropic/claude-opus-5-5`):
No-image: `KNSxx3s` 0.0 (f2p 5/9; overlay ×3, fence Z), `hxqbksk` 0.0 (5/9; overlay ×3, fence Z), `wwL8dZA` 0.0 (4/9; overlay ×3, glass X, fence Z), so 0/3 pass. Every no-image trajectory shows `/app/.harbor_assets/recording.mp4: No such file or directory`.
With-image: `AEURini` **1.0** (9/9 f2p, 9/9 p2p), `Ri5pb59` 0.0 (7/9; glass X, fence Z), `dMNNnzm` 0.0 (6/9; overlay ×3), `tnZgnKu` 0.0 (8/9; glass X), so **exactly 1/4 pass**. Option A is met.
Checksums: the 4 with-image trials and the CB oracle/nop share task checksum `109377229a…`; the 3 no-image trials use `7cb46dfd8d…` (asset-stripped variant). `with_images/task_manifest.json` locks 18 files; all 18 sha256 match the `Tasks/` on disk (0 mismatches). No trial has `exception_info`. Run time (informational): with-image 24.3, 37.1, 20.2, 16.5 min; no-image 12.3, 6.1, 12.0 min (agent execution).
dimensions.fix: None. Note: the passing run found all seven defects; the three failures each missed a different subset (glass + fence, overlay, glass), so the pass is not a single-defect fluke.

dimensions.name: Hardening – Real & Feasible
dimensions.evidence: Seven coherent defects: the upstream overlay polygon offset (issue 15821, fixed by PR 15867, whose code makes up the golden's tile/nodedef part) and six injected one-line bugs of a type real code has: a swapped `nb_triplet` row, swapped facedir ±90 rotations, swapped X entries in `nodebox_tile_dirs`, swapped `rail_kinds` angles, a missing `p2 = cur_node.p;` reset, and swapped wallmounted ±Z rotations. Each fix is the minimal revert a real developer would write. All seven are visible in the clip next to correct counterparts, and `AEURini` (Attempt12) solved all seven from symptom plus clip, as did 2 Attempt8 runs on the same environment, so the task is feasible.

dimensions.name: Gate – Oracle/Nop
dimensions.evidence: CB (Attempt12, checksum `109377229a…`): oracle `USS3TLX` reward 1.0 (f2p 9/9, p2p 9/9), nop `57SU4X7` 0.0 (f2p 0/9, p2p 9/9), no exceptions. Local: `environment/`, `solution/` and `tests/` are byte-identical to Attempt8 (`diff -rq`), so the Attempt8 QC-built image and its runs still apply: nop 0.0 (0/9, 9/9), oracle 1.0 (9/9, 9/9), oracle re-run 1.0 and identical, all with the full stage banners and `reward=`, no "could not apply test.patch". The instruction/task.toml/description edits are not in the verifier path (`task.toml` is blind to the agent, and the tests don't read the instruction). The Attempt12 CB `reward_detail.json` files match the local ones for oracle and nop.
